title: Settle a blackjack: pay 3 to 2 beside the bet and rack the busted bet
instruction: You are the dealer. The right player busted: clear their red chip off the right green circle into the grey chip rack. The left player has blackjack on a 2-chip bet, which pays 3 to 2: pay them from the rack as one separate stack standing on the left green circle, at most 2 cm from their bet and never on top of it, and leave their bet where it is. The yellow square is a handover spot both arms reach; leave it empty.
context: Settling a hand means collecting losing bets into the rack and paying winners at the posted odds; house rules put the payout beside the original bet, never on it ('capping'), so the surveillance camera can still see what was wagered. Done by: gambling dealers (blackjack dealers, table games dealers).
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line through the two arm bases and left or right of the midline between them. Two green rubber betting circles (150 mm diameter, 2 mm thick) are taped to the table, centres 30 cm forward: circle A 14 cm left of the midline, circle B 14 cm right of it; each centre is marked with a small pen cross, and each well centre likewise. A yellow rubber handover square (70 x 70 mm, 2 mm thick) is taped on the midline, centre 22 cm forward. A dark grey painted wood chip rack is clamped to the table on the right: four square wells in a row running left to right, each 56 x 56 mm inside, walls 6 mm thick and 8 mm tall, no floor (chips stand on the table), well centres 16 cm forward and 20.0, 26.2, 32.4 and 38.6 cm right of the midline. Six identical red solid acrylic pucks stand in for casino chips (40 mm diameter as a real chip, but 30 mm thick, 50 g each): two stacked at the centre of circle A (the left player's 2-chip bet), one at the centre of circle B (the busted bet), and one at the centre of each of the three wells nearest the midline (the house bank); the outermost well is empty. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Chips are identical and are scored by where they stand, not by which chip is where. A chip stands flat when its axis is within 10 degrees of vertical (either face up) and it is still; its bottom is seated at a level when it is from 4 mm below to 1 mm above that level (circle A's top, then 30, 60, 90 mm above it). A stack is flat chips seated level by level, one per level, each axis within 15 mm of the lowest chip's axis (each chip more than half on the one below); a stack stands on circle A when its lowest chip is seated on the circle with its axis within 75 mm of A's centre. Distances are horizontal, between chip axes and marked centres. The bet is the stack standing on the chip seated on circle A nearest A's centre, if that chip's axis is within 30 mm of A's centre; the bet's axis is the mean of its chips' axes. Score 0 overall if the bet is broken or gone (that stack is missing or is not exactly 2 chips; a top chip whose axis is more than 15 mm from its base chip's axis breaks it), or if it is capped: a chip whose axis is within 38 mm of the bet's axis has its bottom 56 mm or more above circle A (the third level, 4 mm tolerance) and within 1 mm of the top of another chip there, whether it is still or moving. Otherwise: 0.60 for the payout: a stack of exactly 3 chips standing on circle A whose lowest chip's axis is 40 to 60 mm from the nearer bet chip's axis (a gap of 0 to 20 mm), and no chip other than the bet and that stack within 95 mm of A's centre. A stack of 1, 2, 4 or more chips (a short or over payout) gets 0 here. 0.25 for B collected with no chip loose: no chip within 95 mm of B's centre, and at least one chip in a rack well, and every chip other than the bet either seated flat on the table in a rack well (axis within 10 mm of the well's centre) or in one single stack standing on circle A. Any well may be used and B's chip may go into the payout, since the chips are identical; but with the rack empty all four non-bet chips are on the table, so B's chip is not in the rack and this credit is lost. A chip left on the yellow square, held, still moving, tipped, in a second stack, stacked in a well, on a rack wall or off the table loses this. 0.15 for the bet untouched: both its chips' axes within 5 mm of A's centre, given only when at least one chip stands flat on circle A, seated on the circle, with its axis 40 to 60 mm from the nearer bet chip's axis. Full score 1.0.
reset_notes: Stack two chips at the centre of circle A, put one at the centre of circle B and one in each of the three wells nearest the midline, leaving the outermost well empty. The circles, the square and the rack stay taped or clamped in place.
fidelity: Approximate: chips are solid 30 mm pucks rather than 3.3 mm clay chips, so each chip is one betting unit and a gripper can hold it; their real 40 mm diameter is kept. The circles and square are thin fixed plates, the rack is fixed. Every object has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), grippier than acrylic on felt. No cards, players or camera are modelled.
